_comment: Per-role write permissions. This file is the enforced permission model:
`agentctl guard check` runs it against every agent-authored diff in CI,
so a worker that ignores its prompt still cannot land an out-of-scope
change. A task spec's allowed_paths NARROWS a role; it never widens one.
dotfiles are in agentlib.guard.ALWAYS_FORBIDDEN and cannot be granted here
`deny` is an explicit belt-and-braces denial checked before `write`.
`write` is an allowlist: a path matching nothing in it is refused.

director._role: Human-driven architecture session. Not dispatched by CI and not subject to this file; its changes land as an ordinary human-reviewed PR from a non-agent branch. Listed here so the model is complete.

manager._role: Decides strategy for one task. Reads; does not commit code.

test_agent._role: Writes the failing tests that define the task's contract.
_test_kit_note: `frontend/src/test/**` is the frontend's test kit - the msw handler
factories, fixtures and render helpers a suite is built out of. It is
the test agent's output just as much as a *.test.tsx file is, but the
files are named `users.ts`, `auth.tsx`, `notifications.ts` and so on,
so none of the three patterns above admits one. This repo uses that
directory rather than the `__tests__/**` convention the allowlist
Granted as the whole tree rather than by extension: the kit holds both
.ts and .tsx, and an extension rule would re-create the mismatch it is
here to remove. The code agent is NOT denied this tree - see
_test_kit_and_the_code_agent at the bottom of this file.
_deny_note: There is deliberately no `frontend/src/**/*.tsx` entry here, though the
symmetry with the other trees invites one. `deny` is evaluated BEFORE
`write`, and a component test IS a .tsx file - that pattern denied the
test agent its own output, and every FRONTEND-* task would have
escalated on its first commit. The glob engine has no negation, so the
exception cannot be written into the pattern.
Nothing is lost: `write` above admits only *.test.ts, *.test.tsx and
__tests__/**, so a production .tsx is already refused as 'not in this
role's write allowlist'. tests/test_policy.py pins both halves.

code_agent._role: Implements until the committed tests pass.

distiller._role: Summarises a CI failure from text handed to it in its prompt. Has no repository access at all - see .ai/docs/threat-model.md.

context_maintainer._role: After a green run, records what changed in the one module file the task named. Commits onto the same task branch so the wiki edit lands in the same human-reviewed PR as the code.

_openapi_json_note: backend/openapi.json is the committed frontend/backend contract: the code
agent regenerates it with backend/scripts/export_openapi.py, and CI fails
the build on any drift. It is granted as one exact path rather than a tree,
because a backend route change that does not refresh it silently breaks the
generated TypeScript client - and the agent that changed the route is the
only one positioned to refresh it.
_test_kit_and_the_code_agent: OPEN, and deliberately not decided here. `code_agent.write` admits
`frontend/src/**` and denies only `*.test.ts`/`*.test.tsx`, so the code
agent can write `frontend/src/test/**` - the msw fixtures. That is what
It is a hole in `allow_test_edits_during_impl: false`. A fixture decides
what the server answers, so an implementation that may rewrite one can
weaken the contract without touching a file named *.test.*, and the
discard-the-whole-diff rule never fires. Closing it means adding
Left open because it reverses an explicit, deliberate-looking assertion
about how this system is meant to work, which is a human call. Recorded in
docs/permissions.md's not-enforced list until it is made.
_dependency_changes: docker-compose.yml are denied to the code agent on purpose: adding a dependency
is a supply-chain decision and a Director call, not something a retry loop makes
on attempt 3 to get a test green.
